subject: Retention horizon: default retention windows and EU deletion flows
messages:
From: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@brightbank.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Clarify: EU defaults for request vs output retention + deletion proof

Diego,

Quick question as we're finalizing our security assessment: can you confirm Redwood's default retention behavior for EU-hosted customers? We need clear language around four items for our controls doc:

1) Raw user inputs/prompts (are these persisted, and if so for how long?)
2) Model outputs/completions and embeddings (default retention horizon)
3) Streamed fragments and KV-cache artifacts (do these persist beyond session?)
4) Deletion/erasure process: how to trigger, SLA for deletion, and how we receive proof of deletion (artifact ids, logs, manifest)

Our internal bar is 30 days for anything that counts as PII-able content; if you have a standard offering for 30-day auto-delete in EU that would be ideal to reference. Any attachments that map these to product options would help.

Thanks — Paul
Paul Nguyen
Head of Cloud Security, BrightBank
paul.nguyen@brightbank.com
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@brightbank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: EU defaults for request vs output retention + deletion proof

Paul — thanks for laying this out clearly. Internal note: looping in Kimberly for legal language and Marissa for CS runbook.

Short answer (hosted Redwoods in EU region):
- Requests/prompts (user-submitted text): persisted by default for a 14-day diagnostic buffer, then purged automatically unless customer opts into longer capture for debugging or evals.
- Final outputs & embeddings: retained by default for 90 days (baseline) to support troubleshooting, billing reconciliation, and model-quality monitoring.
- Streamed fragments & KV-cache: streaming buffers are ephemeral and are flushed within 48 hours; KV-cache entries used for session acceleration are retained up to 14 days by default and are excluded from long-term analytics unless flagged.
- Deletion/erasure process: customers can request account-level erasure from Console or via support ticket. Standard hosted erasure SLA is 7 business days from a verified request. Proof of deletion provided as a signed manifest with job id and a list of removed object keys (S3-style), plus a retention-change event id we record in the audit trail.

Attached is a compact mapping (retention_matrix_v2.xlsx) that matches product toggles to these windows.

Caveats and exceptions:
- Billing/audit logs required for invoicing and platform availability diagnostics are retained for 365 days and are not erased as part of a standard content erasure request (we can discuss scoped exceptions with Legal).
- For Private deployments (VPC/on-prem), retention defaults are customer-controlled — Redwood does not enforce automatic deletion unless contractually enabled.
- Temporary holds (legal or incident response) can extend retention; those are logged and require an internal approval flow.

Next steps: Kimberly, can you confirm the legal phrasing we should use back to BrightBank? Marissa, can you draft the CS runbook snippet that explains how to generate the signed manifest for proof of deletion?

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: retention_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet mapping toggles -> retention windows)
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: EU defaults for request vs output retention + deletion proof

Diego — high level looks good. A few legal clarifications to include before sending externally: 

- Wording for the customer-facing doc: 'By default, Redwood retains user-submitted requests for a short diagnostic window (14 days) and final outputs for 90 days. Customers may enable shorter or longer retention via account settings or contractual amendment. Billing and infrastructure audit logs are retained for 365 days and excluded from content erasure requests unless otherwise specified in the agreement.'

- Erasure proof: we provide an erasure manifest containing job id, list of object keys (redwood:// ids), timestamp, and SHA256 of the manifest. The manifest is signed with our internal signing key and stored in the customer's audit bucket for 180 days as evidence. Customer can download this from the Console or request via support.

- Private deployments: emphasize that 'customers retain operational control over retention parameters and must implement deletion workflows for on-prem or VPC-hosted data; Redwood can provide automation packs but does not modify customer-hosted storage.'

- Exception language: add 'retention may be extended for compliance holds, billing, or incident response; any extension will be recorded in the audit log with approver id and reason.'

I'll attach a quick diagram of the erasure flow (brightbank_erasure_flow.drawio) and a one-paragraph legal blurb you can paste into the reply. Marissa — please confirm CS play for generating the signed manifest and whether we need Customer SSO verification step.

Kimberly Park
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@brightbank.com>
Cc: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: EU defaults for request vs output retention + deletion proof

Paul — thanks for the patience. Below is the concise customer-facing summary and next steps; full matrix and erasure flow attached.

Customer-facing summary (BrightBank, EU region):
- Requests/prompts: default diagnostic buffer is 14 days; data is then purged automatically unless you enable longer capture for debugging/evals.
- Final outputs & embeddings: retained by default for 90 days. This baseline supports troubleshooting, billing reconciliation, and quality evaluation.
- Streamed fragments & KV-cache: streaming buffers expire rapidly (48 hours); KV-cache entries up to 14 days by default. These caches are not part of the long-term analytics unless explicitly opted in.
- Erasure & proof: Account erasure can be initiated from the Console or support. Standard hosted erasure SLA is 7 business days. Proof is delivered as a signed manifest (job id, list of removed object ids, manifest SHA256) accessible from the Console and retained for 180 days for audit purposes.

Exceptions and notes:
- Billing and audit logs: retained 365 days and excluded from standard content erasure. We can discuss narrower scopes by contract.
- Private/VPC deployments: retention is customer-managed; Redwood provides automation but does not perform remote deletes without express configuration.

Attached: retention_matrix_v2.xlsx (mapping of toggles to windows), brightbank_erasure_flow.drawio (flow diagram). Also linking the working doc: https://drive.redwood/release/retention-matrix-v2

If you want a formal letter or specific contract language for procurement, Kimberly can provide that paragraph and we can add it to a SOW. Otherwise, if a 30-day baseline is required, we can propose a 30-day hosted profile (Account Setting: content.retention_profile=eu-30) — that would be a paid configuration change and we can scope with Procurement.

Next step: Paul, confirm whether BrightBank needs the 30-day profile or if the 90-day baseline is acceptable; Kimberly to provide legal blurb if you want that in writing. Marissa will follow up with the CS runbook once she confirms the manifest generation steps.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
